A seeded shuffle with three limits: the same band at least 3 slots apart, the same city at most 3 in a row, Mixing also frees us from one bias in past data: weekday won't be tied to a band or a city, so we can later compare slots fairly.

Full-song links

The answer differs by platform, because only Facebook and LinkedIn will carry one. LinkedIn is the one we test.

PlatformWhat worksWhat I'd doEvidence
YouTube ShortsLinks in descriptions and comments aren't clickable. The "Related video" field is, but it needs the channel's primary owner to verify.No link, as you decided. "Full song on our channel" in the description.Official YouTube's help pages state the rule. They give no effect on reach or clicks.
FacebookA caption link is clickable. I checked on a past reel on the web, not in the app. It sits behind "See more" unless it's near the top.Keep it in the caption as a tracked link, moved to the second line so it shows before the cut-off. No comment needed, so it can be fully scheduled.Weak All 19 videos since 14 Sep had a link, so we have nothing to compare, and I found no reel-specific study. Reports of a Meta test capping Pages at 2 link posts a month are second-hand and conflict. We've posted 34 captions with links since 1 Sep, so we aren't being blocked. I'll switch to first comments if a notice appears.
LinkedInLinks work in the post and in comments. Posts can't schedule a comment.Test it with tracked links: half in the post, half in the first comment.Weak Published studies disagree, from about 19% to 60% less reach for a link in the post, against 14% more interactions in one study, and LinkedIn denies a penalty. A first comment seems to lose less, about 11% to 15%, in small tests. None is specific to video. Our own data can't say: LinkedIn metrics stop at 13 Oct and the ledger holds few captions.
InstagramCaption and comment links aren't clickable without a paid plan. The bio link goes to the site."Full song on our page." The song is already posted there, so nobody has to leave.No test Comment-to-DM tools exist, but I wouldn't add one at this size.
TikTokCaption links aren't clickable. A bio link needs a Business account or, by most reports, 1,000 followers."Full song on our page." No URL.Moderate Full songs there get a median 696 views against 268 for short clips (p under 0.001), so sending people to the one on TikTok suits it anyway.

The LinkedIn link test

  • The two arms: the link in the post on one, "Full song in the first comment" on the other. Everything else stays the same: slot, tags and caption wording.
  • Assignment: each consecutive pair of slots gets one of each arm, drawn at random in advance and shown in the order table, so the arms stay balanced over time. The 11 reels give 5 in the post and 6 in the first comment.
  • What gets compared: impressions and views 7 days after each post, and tracked clicks by arm. If reach drops but more people reach the song, that's still useful, so we need both. I fix this now so the result can't be picked afterwards.
  • What it can show: a big difference only. From our 5 measured LinkedIn videos, 6 against 6 would catch a true halving of impressions about 24% of the time, and a 20% drop about 11%; 5 against 5 is a little worse. That estimate is itself rough. If the arms look about equal, the answer is that any difference is too small to see at this size, and I'd keep the link in the post because it needs no live session.
  • What it needs: PR 230 merged, LinkedIn signed in to read reach, and a session just after each first-comment slot.

Other platforms: I'm not testing Facebook. Our views vary too much: caption against comment on 6 reels each would catch a true 20% drop only about 17% of the time, and a comment would mean a live session at every slot.

How we measure YouTube hits

  • Daily view counts, running since 7 Nov: every upload's total views, captured daily. Songs whose reels haven't gone out yet act as the comparison for those that have. This shows the combined lift from all platforms, and it's rough: the numbers are small, and a release or share can move a song's views. Facebook's median is 134 views.
  • Tracked links: clicks by song and placement on Facebook and LinkedIn, in PostHog. They count clicks rather than watches, and they're an upper bound because a scanner posing as a browser can't be told apart. The link shows our domain rather than youtu.be, and I'll compare the counts with what LinkedIn and Facebook report.
  • YouTube Studio traffic sources: views of each full song by source, such as Shorts, Facebook and LinkedIn. Links opened in phone apps may land under "direct or unknown". I'd read it 7 days after each reel.

Why these slots

Instagram is where a slot can matter most: its median video got 667 views against Facebook's 134 since 14 Sep. Facebook views before 14 Sep are excluded because the Meta app was unpublished then and hid those reels.

Instagram video views by publishing hour, Brisbane time, from Business Suite on 7 Nov. Each dot is one post; the bar and number mark the median of posts at least 7 days old. Hollow dots are younger: good 4 u at 23:43 and Mustang Sally at 00:13, which can't yet be compared. Hover a dot for the post.

Your morning rule from 15 Sep (YouTube 07:30, Facebook 09:00) is not what I propose: the numbers don't favour mornings on Instagram or Facebook. The last two Instagram posts went out around midnight; I'd stop that. Say if you'd still rather keep YouTube in the morning, since it costs nothing there.

Audience: Instagram followers (252) are 33% Brisbane, 20% Sydney, 13% Melbourne and about 67% aged 25 to 44. Facebook is under Meta's threshold for demographics.

What to expect: medians for clips of a minute or less are about 640 views on Instagram (n=14), 460 on YouTube Shorts (n=8), 270 on TikTok (n=22) and 85 on Facebook (n=6). TikTok is the weak spot: full songs there get 696 (n=27), with p under 0.001. On YouTube it runs the other way, Shorts 460 against full songs 172. On Instagram length makes no clear difference. All of these views depend far more on the post than the hour: the top of the range is 2,070 on Instagram.

What it takes each week

  • It schedules Reels natively for both Facebook and Instagram from one composer, with separate captions through "Customize post". That fixes the Instagram slot problem: no session has to be alive at publish time.
  • You drag each reel in. Its security rules block our Blob fetch, and this session's browser refuses uploads over 50 MB. The reels are 74 to 105 MB. TikTok and LinkedIn need your drag too. YouTube doesn't: its file comes from our storage. That's 3 drags per reel, 33 for these 11. I fill in everything else.
  • TikTok only schedules 10 days ahead, so the first sitting covers it through Mon 16 Nov and later reels follow in weekly sittings. Anything scheduled on TikTok can't be edited. How far ahead Business Suite goes is unchecked, and I'll confirm it on the first reel.
  • YouTube gets a 2160x3840 render, and every other platform gets the 1080x1920 file. It's an upscale: each vertical window holds at most 1215x2160 real pixels, so it adds no detail. What it may buy is YouTube's handling, because 4K uploads are widely reported to get a better codec and more bitrate. That's unverified, and a test upload would show it.
  • One step needs a live session around the slot: the LinkedIn first comment on the reels in that arm. If nobody's on at that time, I do it later the same day.
  • Collaborators are unconfirmed on scheduled Reels. I'll check on the first one. If the composer doesn't offer them, I add them on instagram.com after each post publishes, which needs that session signed in. The web route takes 3.
  • Whether the Reels composer takes a custom cover isn't checked yet: it needs a video loaded. If not, I'll tell you before Canvanauts is scheduled.

The loop

  • Six reels are rotated so the loop continues the music: Canvanauts, Amakazaam!, V2 Voyagers, All Coming Back, No One Knows and Everlong. At the loop point, sample steps in five of them are ordinary for that reel. Canvanauts' is in its top 0.1%, so listen for a tick.
  • Sultans of Swing measured differently. It's rotated too, with a step at its loop point larger than all but 0.001% of the reel's, and a 12 dB level change in 10 ms. You listened and marked it fine.
  • Four play straight through, so their loop is a hard cut: good 4 u, The Chain, Say It Ain't So and Covered in Chrome.
  • The logo returns on each loop, over the first 4.5 s of every replay, because it's burned in. Platforms that auto-replay will show it each time.
  • Nothing is known yet about the platforms. Each re-encodes the audio and restarts the player its own way, and I can't hear the result. On the first post I'll report what each player does, and I need your ears on a phone for any gap or click. You chose to stage without waiting for that check, and TikTok's scheduled posts can't be edited. Canvanauts will be the first look at a rotated loop, and good 4 u on Wednesday at a hard cut.

The queue and what comes next

  • Nothing else is queued. Facebook scheduled posts: none. TikTok drafts: none. Business Suite Planner this month: only Meta's suggested times, no scheduled posts. Mustang Sally went out 6 Nov.
  • Paint It Black and Barracuda have no dates. Both are still in audio. Each would take a slot when approved, and its reel would follow its release.
  • More reels: Monday, Wednesday and Friday have room for 7 more slots by Fri 18 Dec, including Wed 2 Dec. Past that, either run into January or add Sunday 14:00 Brisbane, a Meta active time but only 28 hours before Monday's slot, which is the kind of gap that did worse (weak evidence).
